correctness.rationale: For any n>=3, 4<=k<=n+1, 1<p<infinity, the four constructed dual unit vectors all lie in the plane w_1+w_2=c. Their coordinate-power inverse images are primal unit vectors. The exact determinant is -2 a^2 T (1-2^(2-q)), where a,T>0, so their affine rank is 3 exactly when p!=2; dual rank is 2. Adding e_4,...,e_(k-1) raises primal rank to k-1 while keeping dual rank <=k-2. At p=2 J is the Euclidean identity. Every nonstandard step is elementary and explicitly proved in RESULT.md; verify.py independently checks 44 finite examples but is not a proof.

originality.rationale: A source-level implication comparison found no covering classification of RP_k for all real ell_p^n, every 1<p<infinity, n>=3 and 4<=k<=n+1. Durand–Liang–Zhang define RP_k, prove it for Euclidean norms and construct exceptional smooth norms, then pose classification as Question 1. Icking et al. exhibit multiple circumcenters for exponent 4 but their accessible abstract supplies neither this all-p result nor a duality-rank determinant. Searches across the published mathematical-record index and the accessible 26 earlier claims returned no equivalent. Full older-paper access remains a residual risk, not a uniqueness claim.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 article explicitly asks to characterize RP_k, and the theorem completely classifies the central real ell_p^n family across all dimensions n>=3, all k>=4 and all smooth exponents p. The determinant witnesses an exact non-Hilbert threshold including exponents arbitrarily close to 2, while the Hilbert branch is positive. This goes beyond a single existence example, finite enumeration or gratuitous invariant; its limit to RP_k rather than medial-axis nonrectifiability is explicit.
